Date January 19, 1934.

Subject (in full) The strength of the foreign units in Shanghai.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by D. S. Umemoto.

In connection with the attached translation from the
"Shanghai Mainichi" dated December 14, 1933, under the heading
"Ten thousand soldiers and marines of various nations defend
Shanghai", Mr. Oki, reporter of the paper, states that the
figures of the strength of the foreign units in Shanghai
mentioned therein were based upon reports appearing in local
newspapers and upon information secured during the course of
his visits to various places. However, he cannot state that the
figures are correct not as they had been obtained from any official
source.

It is noteworthy of mention that Captain Otorii, Commander
of the Japanese Company, S.V.C., is an employee of the Mainichi.

C.W.

主题（全称）上海外侨部队之兵力。

制作人：D. S. Umemoto。转呈人：D. S. Umemoto。

关于随附的1933年12月14日《上海每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）题为“各国万名海陆军保卫上海”的译文，该报记者Oki先生称，文中提及的上海外侨部队兵力数字系依据当地报纸的报道及其在各处走访期间获取的信息。然而，他无法声明这些数字是准确的，因为它们并非取自任何官方来源。

值得一提的是，上海义勇队（S.V.C.）日本连连长Otorii上尉是《每日新闻》的雇员。

December 14, 1933. Afternoon Translation.

LATE LORI

NUMBER OF JAPANESE SERVANT GIRLS

The total number of Japanese geisha girls,
dancing partners, waitresses and prostitutes in
Shanghai was reported to be 1080 on December 13, 1933.
They are classified as follows :-
Geisha girls 220
Dancing partners 200
Waitresses 480
Prostitutes. 180

TEN THOUSAND SOLDIERS AND MARINES OF VARIOUS NATIONS
DEFEND SHANGHAI

Shanghai is a civilized international city.
The maintenance of the peace and order in Shanghai has
been preserved by the navies and armies of various
countries. During times of trouble many warships of
various countries defend the harbour while on land 2,000
Japanese marines under the command of Rear-Admiral Uno,
1,600 American marines under the command of Colonel
Beaumont, 1,165 British soldiers and 2,100 volunteers
under the command of Colonel Thackaray and 1,900 French
soldiers in the French Concession under the command of
Colonel Frison , protect the residents.
The Japanese landing force is now the leading
defence unit in Shanghai since two battalions of the British
soldiers departed and Rear-Admiral Uno is the leading officer
in Shanghai.
Chinese soldiers are not allowed to come within
the limits decided in the terms of the Sino-Japanese
armistice. Accordingly the International Settlement
is guarded by the International force and the French
Concession by the French soldiers.
The Shanghai Defence Commission is to decide
which parts of the Settlement will be defended by the
various forces. There are indications that Shanghai is
an international port awaiting further development
by the various nations.

NIPEO

TWO DEPUTY COMMISSIONERS AND TWO SUPERINTENDENTS
TO BE APPOINTED

It is reported that at yesterday's meeting
of the S.M.C. it was resolved that two Deputy Police
Commissioners (one Japanese and one Chinese) and two
Superintendents (one Japanese and one Chinese) should be
appointed.
It is reported that Mr. Tajima, Japanese
A.C.P.,will be promoted to the newly created post of
Japanese Deputy Commissioner and Mr. Uehara, Superintendent,
will take over Mr. Tajima's position, while the latter's
post may be filled by a newcomer to the Force.

1933年12月14日。下午译文。

LATE LORI

日本艺妓人数

据1933年12月13日报道，上海的日本艺妓、舞伴、女侍应生和妓女总数为1080人。分类如下：-
艺妓 220
舞伴 200
女侍应生 480
妓女 180

各国万名海陆军保卫上海

上海是一座文明的国际都市。
上海的和平与秩序由各国海陆军维持。在动荡时期，各国许多军舰保卫港口，而在陆地上，由宇野少将指挥的2,000名日本海军陆战队、由Beaumont上校指挥的1,600名美国海军陆战队、由Thackaray上校指挥的1,165名英国士兵和2,100名义勇队员，以及由Frison上校指挥的位于法租界的1,900名法国士兵，保护着居民。
自两个营的英国士兵撤离后，日本登陆部队目前成为上海的主要防御单位，宇野少将是上海的最高级军官。
根据中日停战协定的条款，中国士兵不得进入划定的界限内。因此，公共租界由国际部队守卫，法租界由法国士兵守卫。
上海防务委员会将决定租界的哪些区域由各支部队防守。有迹象表明，上海是一个等待各国进一步开发的国际港口。

NIPEO

将任命两名副警务处长和两名督察长

据报道，在昨日的工部局会议上，决议任命两名副警务处长（一名日本人，一名中国人）和两名督察长（一名日本人，一名中国人）。
据报道，日本助理警务处长田岛先生（Mr. Tajima）将晋升为新设的日本副警务处长职位，督察长上原先生（Mr. Uehara）将接替田岛先生的职位，而田岛先生原来的职位可能由警队的一名新人填补。

that the departure of Brigadier Fleming and the 2nd
Battalion The Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders had

THE CHINA PRESS. WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 13, 1933

Defense Area Shift
Rumored For City

Re-Deal Among Foreign Troops In Settlement
Mooted Question Among Military Moguls
But Increase In Power Of Japanese
Forces In Central Now Hinted

Is there going to be a re-shuffle of defense areas in the International Settlement protected by various foreign troop units—including those of British, American, and Japanese governments and Shanghai Volunteer Corps forces—stationed in Shanghai? This is a question that many a local Chinese and foreign resident would like to have answered.

The Shanghai Defense Committee, whose membership is made up of commanding officers of foreign troops and the S.V.C. here, knows—but it won't tell. Recently the question has been delved into by a CHINA PRESS representative. Several of the commanders have replied to queries that such a re-arrangement was "news" to them. Still others have stated that "something of the sort has been decided upon" but because of a mutual agreement among committee members, they said they were not at liberty to divulge details. Officers at S. V. C. headquarters—Colonel Thoms could not be interviewed on the subject—denied any knowledge of such a plan and added that if there were a "re-shuffle" in effect or contemplated, that it would not be released to the press or the public. Information of this nature must be kept secret as releasing it might be to the advantage of "the enemy" in the event of trouble in Shanghai, it was said.

S.V.C. Growing

It is also thought possible that recent attempts to increase the membership of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps—through appeals by S.V.C. officials to local foreign firms—are intended to make the corps membership large enough to fill the depleted ranks of Shanghai British forces.

Not the least interesting of rumors circulated in the local foreign community recently, is that which says that an agreement has been made which will permit the Japanese Naval Landing Party to patrol the central district of the International Settlement formerly patrolled by other foreign troop detachments, in the event Shanghai is threatened with military invasion or danger in the future.

Fukien Trouble At Bottom

It is virtually certain that something along this line has been discussed and is possibly now in force. It is reported in various quarters that the subject has been brought into the local military spotlight as a result of the national unrest caused by trouble now existing in Fukien.

In view of the recent retirement from Shanghai of a battalion of British troops, now stationed at Hongkong, it is obvious that the area formerly patrolled by the British forces here must be taken over by the troops of some other government now stationed in the Settlement, unless the Shanghai Defense Committee is relying on the plan of rushing in troops from Hongkong in event of trouble. This is believed unlikely as arrangements for quarters, instruction in familiarizing these forces with local conditions and the fact that they might also be needed in the north at the same time, would all go to work to the disadvantage of adequate protection of Shanghai by foreign military units.

Japanese In Central?

During and since the Shanghai invasion early in 1932 the Japanese have patrolled Hongkew and Yangtsepoo districts. The question now, which no one in authority seems willing or able to answer, is, will the Japanese be permitted to expand the area they now protect? Reports are to be heard on all sides in Shanghai that the Japanese will be allowed to patrol the central district if the city is again endangered.

At the time of the "Shanghai incident" Volunteer Corps forces were massed along north Settlement roads as far west as Myburgh Road to prevent either the Japanese or Chinese troops from entering the foreign-controlled area. American forces generally confined their protective activities between Myburgh and Kiaochow Roads on the north boundary of the Settlement along Soochow Creek, while the British held forth between Kiaochow Road and Jessfield Park, and as far south as Amherst Avenue and Avenue Haig.

French troops were restricted to defending the French Concession on all sides.

At the present time there are approximately 1,900 American marines in Shanghai, while the British have 1,600; Japanese, 2,140; French, 1,600 to 1,700, and S.V.C., 2,100 (which number officials of the Corps are now trying to increase).

（批：DI, Please verify the contents of this article and report. JH）

《字林西报》。1933年12月13日，星期三

防区变动
传闻将涉及全市

租界内外军重新部署
军事巨头们讨论中的议题
但暗示日军在中央区的权力将增强

由驻扎在上海的各外国部队单位——包括英国、美国和日本政府部队以及上海义勇队部队——保护的公共租界，其防区是否将进行重新调整？这是许多本地中外居民希望得到解答的问题。

上海防务委员会的成员由驻沪外国部队指挥官和上海义勇队指挥官组成，他们知情——但不愿透露。近日，《字林西报》代表对此问题进行了深入探究。几位指挥官回复询问时称，此类重新安排对他们来说是“新闻”。另一些人则表示，“已决定采取类似措施”，但由于委员会成员之间有默契，他们表示无权泄露细节。上海义勇队总部的官员——Thoms上校未能就此主题接受采访——否认知晓此类计划，并补充说，如果正在实施或计划进行“重新调整”，也不会向媒体或公众发布。据说，此类信息必须保密，因为一旦上海发生动乱，泄露信息可能会使“敌人”受益。

上海义勇队正在壮大

也有人认为，近期上海义勇队官员呼吁本地外籍商行增加队员人数的尝试，可能是为了使义勇队人数足够多，以填补上海英军兵力减少后的空缺。

最近在本地外籍社区流传的谣言中，最有趣的莫过于称已达成一项协议，允许日本海军登陆部队在未来上海面临军事入侵或危险时，巡逻以前由其他外国分遣队巡逻的公共租界中央区。

福建事变是根源

几乎可以肯定，此类事宜已经过讨论，并且可能现已生效。各方消息称，由于目前福建事变引起的全国性动荡，该问题已成为本地军事关注的焦点。

鉴于最近一个营的英军从上海撤出（现驻香港），显然，以前由驻沪英军巡逻的区域必须由目前驻扎在租界的其他国家部队接管，除非上海防务委员会依赖在发生动乱时从香港调兵的计划。但这被认为不太可能，因为营房安排、让部队熟悉当地情况的训练，以及他们可能同时需要在北方服役的事实，都不利于外国军事单位对上海提供充分的保护。

日军进入中央区？

在1932年初上海战事期间及之后，日军一直巡逻虹口和杨浦区。现在的问题是，当局似乎无人愿意或能够回答：日军是否会被允许扩大其目前的保护区？上海各处均有传闻称，如果城市再次面临危险，日军将被允许巡逻中央区。

在“上海事变”期间，义勇队部队沿租界北部道路集结，西至迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road），以防止日军或中国军队进入外国人控制区。美军通常将其保护活动限制在租界北界苏州河沿岸的迈尔西爱路和胶州路之间，而英军则负责胶州路至兆丰公园（Jessfield Park）以及南至安赫斯特大道（Amherst Avenue）和海格大道（Avenue Haig）的区域。

法军仅限于防守法租界四周。

目前，上海约有1,900名美国海军陆战队士兵，英军1,600名；日军2,140名；法军1,600至1,700名；上海义勇队2,100名（该队官员正试图增加此人数）。

（批注：DI，请核实本文内容并报告。JH）
